reply.recognition: Recognize the supplied source as the public UCI Appliances Energy Prediction dataset (UCI 374), with the listed 2017 Candanedo et al. paper. I recognize the dataset and its stated prediction purpose; I do not rely on a remembered result beyond the supplied documentation.
reply.summary: Three candidate additions address operational measurement or intervention rather than another aggregate load predictor. Select I1: test whether aggregate-load-triggered temporary submetering identifies the contributors to high-use intervals more efficiently than equal-budget random submetering. The file supports defining aggregate event windows and time strata, but it contains no appliance-circuit labels, occupancy, or interventions, so it cannot establish attribution or savings.

candidates.title: Trigger temporary submetering on household load events
candidates.question: At equal metering time, does activating synchronized circuit submeters during aggregate appliance-load events reveal the circuits responsible for more high-use energy than activating them in randomly selected intervals?
candidates.new_claim: A two-stage monitoring policy may improve the yield of scarce circuit-level metering for identifying contributors to high-use intervals; this is a measurement-efficiency hypothesis, not an energy-saving mechanism.
candidates.input_delta: The supplied data contains aggregate Appliances Wh every 10 minutes but no appliance-level readings. Add a prospective comparison of event-triggered and equal-budget random windows with synchronized circuit-level Wh labels.
candidates.domain_value: A building-energy team could use limited portable or temporary submeters to find which circuits merit follow-up control or maintenance, instead of collecting circuit data continuously.
assumptions: Aggregate Appliance Wh is available promptly enough to trigger the next measurement window.
Circuit submeters can be synchronized to the 10-minute whole-home meter.
A high-use interval may have a more concentrated or otherwise more actionable circuit contribution than a typical interval; this is unverified.
variables_and_units: Aggregate Appliances energy, Wh per 10-minute interval
Circuit-level energy, Wh per synchronized 10-minute interval
Metering effort, number of monitored intervals
Peak-contributor yield, share of metered high-use intervals where the leading circuit and its Wh are recovered
candidates.testable_prediction: Using a trigger threshold fixed from an initial calibration period and the same number of monitored intervals, event-triggered sampling will identify a leading circuit accounting for at least half of aggregate appliance Wh in more held-out aggregate high-use intervals per metered interval than random sampling. The 50% criterion and trigger rule must be fixed before collection.
candidates.alternative: High aggregate intervals may combine many circuits or have unstable contributors, so targeted sampling may not identify a dominant circuit more often than random sampling; any apparent gain may also be confined to particular times or seasons.
candidates.discriminating_test: In a prospective single-home pilot, collect synchronized aggregate and circuit-level Wh continuously as evaluation truth, but score two pre-registered equal-budget sampling schedules: (a) activate the limited analysis/inspection budget in intervals triggered by aggregate Appliances exceeding a threshold learned only from the prior calibration period, and (b) activate it in randomly selected intervals matched by calendar week and time-of-day. On held-out weeks, compare the fraction of aggregate top-decile intervals for which the sampled circuit data identifies the leading circuit and whether it contributes at least 50% of appliance Wh. Report paired week-level differences and uncertainty; do not treat 10-minute rows as independent homes.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Partly. The supplied 10-minute aggregate series and dates can define candidate trigger windows and matched time strata, but cannot evaluate circuit attribution or the 50% criterion.
candidates.required_new_data: For one or more homes, collect synchronized whole-home Appliances Wh and circuit-level Wh (one value per circuit per 10-minute interval) over calibration and held-out weeks; retain the full circuit record during the pilot as evaluation truth, plus activation flags for each schedule. Multiple homes are needed before claiming generalization across households.
candidates.failure_condition: The idea fails its primary prediction if equal-budget event-triggered sampling does not increase the held-out fraction of high-use intervals with a correctly identified leading circuit relative to week/time-matched random sampling, or if the advantage disappears across held-out weeks. A result in one home would still not support household-wide generalization.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query: household residential energy monitoring event-triggered submetering sampling versus random or uniform circuit-level metering, evaluated for identification of high-load appliance contributors.

candidates.title: Use room thermal recovery traces to target ventilation checks
candidates.question: After comparable outdoor-temperature changes, do room-specific temperature recovery traces identify periods when measured ventilation or air exchange is unusually high, beyond the information in airport weather alone?
candidates.new_claim: A room-to-room thermal recovery signature could help schedule ventilation diagnostics, but only if it agrees with direct air-exchange measurement under controlled operating conditions.
candidates.input_delta: The file supplies 10-minute room temperatures T1-T9, north-side outdoor T6, airport T_out, and weather, but no ventilation, window, or HVAC-state labels. Add direct air-exchange measurements and logged operating states to test a diagnostic use of thermal response traces.
candidates.domain_value: A validated signature could prioritize building-envelope or ventilation checks when continuous airflow sensing is unavailable.
assumptions: Room temperature response contains a measurable ventilation-related component.
Heating, solar gains, occupancy, and sensor placement can be measured or controlled sufficiently to distinguish competing causes.
A single-house observational trace is hypothesis-generating only.
variables_and_units: Room and north-side temperatures T1-T9 and T6, degrees C per 10-minute interval
Airport outdoor temperature T_out, degrees C per 10-minute interval
Air-change rate, h^-1, measured by tracer-gas decay
Window/HVAC operating state, categorical with timestamps
candidates.testable_prediction: Within controlled, matched temperature-step trials, a pre-specified room-temperature recovery time will be shorter at higher directly measured air-change rates after accounting for logged HVAC and window states; the association should replicate across rooms or trial days.
candidates.alternative: Thermal mass, internal gains, or control cycling may dominate recovery time, leaving no stable relationship with measured air-change rate.
candidates.discriminating_test: Run repeated controlled trials in the same home with randomized window/ventilation settings, direct tracer-gas air-change measurements in h^-1, and synchronized 10-minute room/outdoor temperatures. Compare recovery-time slopes across settings within room and day; record HVAC state and reject trials with unmeasured operating changes. Use existing rows only to pre-specify candidate rooms and ranges, not as validation of ventilation.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Exploratory thermal traces are available, but validation against ventilation and separation from HVAC, occupancy, and solar gains are not feasible.
candidates.required_new_data: Repeated room-level tracer-gas air-change measurements in h^-1, window and HVAC state logs, and preferably occupancy/solar-gain proxies synchronized with room temperatures; replicate trials over multiple days and homes.
candidates.failure_condition: The proposed diagnostic fails if recovery time does not change consistently with directly measured air-change rate within controlled matched trials, or if HVAC/window state explains the apparent signature better than air exchange.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query: residential room temperature decay or thermal recovery as an indicator of measured air change rate, validated with tracer gas under logged HVAC and window states.

candidates.title: Test occupancy-triggered feedback for flexible household loads
candidates.question: Does brief, privacy-preserving feedback after a high appliance-load interval reduce energy in the next hour without worsening indoor comfort, compared with the same feedback delivered at matched non-event times?
candidates.new_claim: A load-event-timed feedback intervention may shift flexible household appliance use; the timing effect is unknown and must be randomized rather than inferred from observational traces.
candidates.input_delta: The dataset has aggregate Appliances and lights Wh, room climate, and dates, but no occupancy, appliance identity, feedback, or comfort ratings. Add a randomized feedback intervention with those measurements.
candidates.domain_value: If effective and comfortable, an energy team could time low-cost prompts to moments when a household has a meaningful opportunity to defer flexible use.
assumptions: Some high-load intervals include deferrable use rather than fixed or essential loads.
A household can receive and act on a prompt.
A one-home trial estimates an individual response and cannot establish population effects.
variables_and_units: Appliance energy, Wh per 10-minute interval and summed Wh over the next 60 minutes
Prompt assignment and delivery time, binary and timestamp
Occupant comfort, pre-specified ordinal response scale
candidates.testable_prediction: Within-house randomized event-timed prompts will reduce next-hour appliance Wh relative to matched no-prompt event windows without increasing the pre-specified rate of comfort reports outside the acceptable range.
candidates.alternative: Loads may be non-deferrable, prompts may be ignored, or reductions may be rebound into the following hours; event timing may offer no advantage over ordinary prompts.
candidates.discriminating_test: After a baseline period, randomize eligible high-load events within household and time-of-day blocks to event-timed prompt or no prompt, and separately randomize matched non-event prompt windows if testing timing specificity. Measure whole-home appliance Wh continuously, occupancy only with consent, and comfort before and after the next hour. Pre-register the next-hour Wh contrast, rebound window, and comfort threshold.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No. The series describes energy and climate but contains no prompt, occupancy, or comfort data and is observational.
candidates.required_new_data: A consented randomized household pilot with prompt assignment/delivery logs, continuous appliance Wh, occupancy or response availability, and repeated comfort ratings; include several post-prompt hours to measure rebound.
candidates.failure_condition: The intervention fails if event-timed prompts do not reduce next-hour Wh relative to randomized controls, if the effect is offset by rebound within the pre-specified follow-up period, or if comfort worsens beyond the registered limit.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query: randomized event-triggered residential energy feedback prompts versus time-matched prompts or control, measuring appliance energy, comfort, and rebound.

task.deliverable: Critique I1 and return a tightened prospective protocol that fixes the trigger calculation, equal-budget comparator, evaluation outcome, and analysis unit before any data return. Distinguish what the supplied aggregate series can check from what requires new circuit-level labels. If useful, request at most one broker computation and one Crossref search under the run rules; do not treat either as completed evidence.
acceptance: Retain or explicitly revise the I1 hypothesis and its alternative.
Specify a calibration-only aggregate trigger and an equal-count random schedule matched by week and time of day.
Define the circuit-level outcome, 50% threshold, held-out evaluation, and week-level uncertainty without treating rows as independent homes.
State whether the current data can check only event-window coverage or can test attribution; do not claim causal savings or validated attribution from this file.
If requesting search, state what finding would change the protocol; if requesting computation, make it a descriptive feasibility check using supplied DF only.
task.proposed_computation: A broker may compare the date/time distribution and aggregate Appliances Wh captured by a calibration-only threshold schedule versus an equal-count, week/time-matched random schedule using the supplied rows. This checks schedule feasibility and temporal coverage only; it cannot estimate which circuit contributed or validate the attribution hypothesis.
task.proposed_search: If a focused Crossref search is available, check whether household event-triggered submeter schedules have already been compared with equal-budget random sampling for circuit-level identification of high-use contributors. A close prior comparison would narrow the claimed addition to the pre-registered leading-circuit outcome and matched held-out-week protocol; a title alone is not evidence of a result.
